text:
maria: Quick follow-up on slow-path handling at the gateway — when upstream latency > 500ms for streaming we currently buffer and wait. Should the gateway automatically flip to a non-streaming fallback or route to an alternate backend? Thoughts?

sam: prefer hedging to an alternate upstream if available. falling back to non-streaming only when hedging fails. :thinking:

lee: fwiw telemetry shows ~0.4% of requests hit >500ms for models A/B during peak. hedging would increase token egress by ~x2 for those, so cost impact is non-trivial.

lee: sample config sketch:
```
route:
  slowpath_ms: 500
  hedging:
    enabled: true
    max_attempts: 2
    adapt_window_s: 3
  fallback:
    to_non_stream: true
    preserve_partial: true
```

jordan: major concern: switching to non-stream mid-response breaks client streaming contract. we need an explicit client contract or trailer to indicate transition — cannot be silent.

anne: billing q: if gateway hedges to another model, which model gets billed? users expect a single charge.

maria: good catch. proposal: annotate billing with routing breadcrumbs and prorate to the model that produced each token. may need legal/product check but we'll prototype.

sam: also: retries/hedges only safe for idempotent requests. we should expose an explicit header `x-ri-idempotency: safe|unsafe|unknown` so callers can opt-in.

jordan: +1 for header. also tool-calls or side-effecting endpoints must be marked unsafe and never hedged.

lee: practical safety rule: if stream has already emitted >N tokens, don't hedge to avoid duplication and reordering. N=10 seems reasonable for a start.

maria: agreed. Implementation plan notes:
- per-route config flags for hedging and fallback
- client opt-in header for idempotency
- trailers: `x-ri-fallback: non-stream|hedge|none`, and `x-ri-partial: true` when we truncated or resumed
- billing breadcrumbs in tracing header for downstream attribution

deploy-bot: deploy queued: edge/proxy-slowpath-config v2 -> staging at 13:02 UTC

sam: I'll draft an RFC with config semantics, failure modes, and cost analysis.

maria: thanks — follow-ups: sam (RFC draft), lee (telemetry queries + cost calc), jordan (client trailer contract), anne (billing/legal check). pinging @here for awareness :eyes:
